lines: Our emotions are important because they help us survive.
Fear keeps us away from danger.
Anger can scare away our enemies.
And good feelings help us get closer to others.
These emotions work like “programs” in our brains.
When something happens, an emotion starts and controls what we do.
It changes how we pay attention, how we move, and what we remember.
For example, when we meet our enemies, fear makes us focus more on the danger.
Then we can choose to fight or run away.
We also remember this kind of scary event more clearly, so we can stay safe in the future.
Thus, each emotion helps protect us.
If emotions did not help us survive, we would not still have them today.
